findings.title: Rejected devices are cached as successfully admitted
findings.body: TagDevice now propagates the device-limit error to authentication, but tagDeviceUI adds the device ID to the 29-minute local cache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and does not remove it when that call fails. When a new device is rejected because the limit is full, its next request hits that cache and returns nil without checking the store, so Anonymous.Authenticate grants access. Cache only successful admissions (and ensure concurrent requests cannot treat an in-progress admission as successful), and add a test that retries a rejected device.

findings.title: Device-limit check and admission are not atomic
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts active devices in one database session and performs the subsequent upsert in another, without any serialization. If the count is one below the limit, concurrent requests with different device IDs can all observe that count and all insert successfully, exceeding the configured limit. This also occurs across Grafana instances sharing the database. Serialize the count-and-admit operation with a database-level mechanism or equivalent cross-instance coordination, and test concurrent admissions at the limit.
